key_insight: Better web agents need targeted practice in reusable skills—not just more tasks. MiniWeb makes those skills measurable in a realistic miniature web.
problem_solved: Overall task success can hide why browser agents fail. MiniWeb helps diagnose weaknesses in specific interaction skills across everyday web workflows.
method: Build MiniWeb: 65 interconnected websites spanning 15 domains for navigation, search, and transactions.
Provide 369 human-annotated tasks labeled with 37 reusable interaction primitives across 7 skill families.
Use skill-level annotations to analyze agent weaknesses beyond task completion; the provided abstract does not include benchmark results.
impact: Practitioners can use skill-level diagnostics to target training and evaluation more precisely. This could support more reliable generalist web agents, though performance gains are not reported in the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Miniature web map showing interconnected sites across 15 domains.
Skill hierarchy: 7 families branching into 37 interaction primitives.
Annotated workflow showing navigation → search → transaction.
Conceptual skill heatmap illustrating how task failures can reveal specific weaknesses.
paper_title: Back to Basics: A Skill-Centric Approach to Generalist Web Agents
paper_authors: Minh Pham-Dinh, Md Farhan Ishmam, Hernan Yupanqui, Reaz Hassan Joarder, Kenneth Marino
